title: A permit to finish a permit
question: How often does someone have to take out a new permit only to close, renew or revive an earlier one?
finding: Since 2015, 8,860 building permits (2.6% of all filed) were taken out only to get a final inspection on, renew or reinstate an earlier permit; the earlier permit was a median 4.4 years old, and 44% were five or more years old. 541 lots needed three or more such permits. Of full-review permits issued for filings from 2012 to 2019, 6% were later named by a finishing or renewal permit and 23% still show no final sign-off.
how: Building permits filed since 2015 whose stated purpose says 'to obtain final inspection', 'to complete work approved under', or to renew, extend or reinstate a permit or application (street-space renewals left out). The age is the filing date of the new permit minus the date built into the oldest earlier permit number it quotes.
limits: A building permit lapses if work stops or is never signed off, and the records show the fix is a fresh permit with its own fee. Many of these are owners tidying up old paperwork before a sale, which is ordinary. The data cannot say why the first permit lapsed, whether an inspector was unavailable, or what the second permit cost. Wording varies, so some are missed.
